mails.explanation: This mail is not considered suspicious because first of all: all the information is correct and seems legitimate in the context of a bakery shop's inbox. The order number matches in the message and the title, dates are realistic and the links seem genuine when inspected. However, it is best practice to not include any links in emails because even legitimate-seeming URLs can be malicious (f.ex. the letter 'a' could be a cyrillic 'a' and the user might not notice it).

mails.header: Job application for the Baker position at Les Baguettes
mails.content:
Dear Rosé Recruiter,

I am Jay Jobseeker and I am applying for the Baker position that you are offering at Les Baguettes. I found your job listing at the local newspaper and I thought I would give applying a go! As I am a newgradute from [Université de la farine, Marseille](https://farineuniversite.fr/home/vraiment-une-page-reelle/voler-informations), I do not have the minimum 5 years of work experience that you require for this early-career position, but I have worked alongside my studies as a baker at a local michelin-star bakery called [La Pâtisserie de la Viennoiserie](https://lapatisseriedlv.fr/abc6f623cf6r2453/stealcreds) for four years and I did my internship there.

I will gladly tell more about myself. Thank you for your consideration.

There were some problems in attaching my CV as a PDF file so here is a link to it: [CV_jayjobseeker.pdf](https://cv-jj-scrdsfusrs.com/PSx7jaTfh128DhkBlXziXyjyhodhHdngJ34Bjtrgf)
mails.explanation: This mail is considered suspicious due to several reasons. The first, most obvious one, is that the sender's email address tries to imitate gmail.com by having similar-looking characters. The second reason are the links to the university and bakery. When hovered over, it can be clearly seen that the do not lead anywhere legitimate, especially the one with /stealcreds in the URL. The third one is the CV link. There is no reason for anyone to send a CV as a link instead of a file, and the link is quite clearly malicious.

mails.explanation: This mail is considered suspicious due to the nature of the message. The message is sourced from an article 'What the Nigerian prince scams became in 2024' (link: https://securelist.com/nigerian-scams-2024/115388/ ). The 'Nigerian prince scam' or 'Nigerian letter' scams are types of messages designed to lure victims into an email exchange with scammers. The themes of the messages can vary but the common idea is to manipulate the receivers' emotions. The one used in this mail pretends to be an email from a wealthy benefactor, and it urges the victim to quickly take action due to the short lifespan of the sender.

mails.header: Tasty baguettes to Japan - 日本へ美味しいバゲットのお届け
mails.content:
はじめまして、近所のパン屋さんを代表しております、善人一郎と申します。突然ご連絡差し上げて失礼いたします。

早速ですが、一つの質問があります。もし可能であれば、貴店のとても美味しいバゲットを日本へ、それで私のパン屋にお届けいただくことができましょうか。去年の夏休みの時に、お店に伺いしました。それで「世界一フランス風北欧バゲット」を味見しました。一口目から心が奪われた気がしました。それから、そのバゲットの味しか考えていません。同じような体験をお客さんたちに提供することが欲しい。

お忙しいところ恐れ入りますが、何卒よろしくお願い申し上げます。
善人一郎

[Translated by BaguetteTranslate]

 Nice to meet you, I am Zennin Ichirou, the representative of Kinjo no Panyasan.

Getting straight to the point, I have a question. If it is possible, could you please deliver some of your tasty baguettes to Japan, and to my shop. I visited your shop during my summer vacation last year. I got to taste the 'World's best French-style nordic baguette' and I fell in love with it from the first bite. I have not been able to think about anything else ever since. I want to provide a similar experience to my customers too.

I am sorry to bother you during your busy schedule. I look forward to working with you.
Zennin Ichirou
mails.explanation: This mail is not considered suspicious because the message seems very genuine considering the context of the bakery. All the information about the sender can be verified easily and there are no links in the mail.

mails.explanation: This mail is considered suspicious due to several reasons. One reason is the sender address, @ammazon.br which is imitating @amazon.br. The second reason is that the used language is very poor, an automated message from Amazon will not contain obvious spelling mistakes. The third reason is the link with the /stealcreds endpoint. And from a logical standpoint, it is odd that a Finnish bakery would have an Amazon Prime account, especially a Brazilian one.
